title: Az-Zalzalah: the quake
hookLine: on that Day the earth tells its news, and an atom's weight of good is seen (Surah 99)

cards: People who've lived through an earthquake describe the same thing first. Not the noise. The ground.

The one thing you never think about, the thing that holds everything up, suddenly moving under your feet. Glasses rattle, then walls, and the floor feels like the deck of a boat. Everything you assumed was solid isn't.
Today's surah opens with the whole earth shaking like that, once and for all. Then it does something tender: it zooms all the way down, to the smallest thing there is.

teach.b: Zalzalah is a word that shakes when you say it: zal-zala, the syllables doubling like a tremor.

teach.h: THE EARTH THROWS OUT ITS BURDENS.
teach.b: The surah begins: when the earth is shaken with its final quake, and throws out its burdens, and a person asks, what's wrong with it? That day it will tell its news. More on that line tomorrow.
Today, the ending, which many Muslims know by heart. In Pickthall's translation: And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then.
The word translated atom is dharrah.

teach.h: DHARRAH — A TINY ANT, A SPECK OF DUST.
teach.b: In the Arabic of the time it meant a tiny ant, or a speck of dust in a sunbeam, the smallest thing a person could see. In the surah's picture, nothing gets lost. Not the big donation, and not the smile at the cashier.
Not the cruel comment, and not the kind one.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ made the same point in a hadith in Bukhari: protect yourself from the Fire, even with half a date given in charity. Half a date.
And in Muslim: don't look down on any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face. This surah turns a corner.
Eighteen days of the shortest surahs, read from the last page of the Qur'an backward, from An-Nas to here. From tomorrow the surahs grow a little longer.
This stretch ends on the right note: an atom of good, seen.

how: Az-Zalzalah is recited in the prayers, and its last two verses on the atom's weight of good and ill are among the most quoted lines in Muslim teaching on small deeds.

o: a flood that covers the whole earth
the earth's last great shaking on that Day
a storm that tears the sky apart

games.q: what's inside the surah — tap the pairs.
p: a tiny ant, a speck of dust
enough to protect from the Fire
a good deed not to look down on

s: only big deeds are counted, in the surah
an atom's weight of good, and of ill, will be seen.
dharrah meant a modern atom when the Qur'an came
it meant a tiny ant or a speck of dust, the smallest thing you could see.
the Prophet said even half a date in charity protects
protect yourself from the Fire, even with half a date (Bukhari).

games.q: you have almost nothing to give today: half a date. what did the Prophet say about it?
o: give it: protect yourself from the Fire even with half a date
eat it; charity is for the rich
games.why: half a date is enough to count (Bukhari). the surah says an atom's weight of good will be seen.

practice: Picture a dharrah: one speck of dust turning in a sunbeam.
Think that small, and find one tiny good you could do in the next hour, a glass of water for someone, a kind reply, picking up one piece of litter, a smile on purpose, and picture yourself doing it.
Make it so small you can't say no.

wordCard.voice: Az-Zalzalah. The quake, the final shaking of the earth, and the surah that says an atom's weight of good will be seen. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the quake, the violent shaking; the doubled syllables echo a tremor.

carryVoice: Your line: an atom of good. The surah says even that small gets seen. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then.

sources.ref: Qur'an 99:1–4 (the quake, the burdens, what's wrong with it)
